capability_claims.description: one-shot voiced line renders live through the Chatterbox service with typed receipt
requested intensity produces measured acoustic arousal via analyze-chatterbox-emotions, not just echoed request fields
session holds bounded mood + speaker across turns; a no-intensity turn keeps the held mood and last tone; speaker-tagged memory recall lands in the receipt
unknown voice / dead service / non-live receipt fail closed with no artifact

tag/knob routing contract survives 50 freshly sampled adversarial scenarios per run: valid tags stay on turbo, tag+intensity conflicts route to base with tags_interpreted=false declared, invented tags never claimed applied, unknown tones/empty text/SSML never crash unbounded

out_of_scope_claims.note: interrupt/barge-in, memory turn-holding, research routing, and wait/delay language are embry-voice-control claims; see its turn rungs (listener-turn-live, embry-chat-static-query-live, research-turn-live) and memory /execution-stats for ETA-driven wait speech

cases.name: tag-opt-out-receipt-proof
command:
OUT=$(mktemp /tmp/cbx-optout-XXXX.json); cd /home/graham/workspace/experiments/agent-skills/skills/chatterbox-speak && ./run.sh speak --text 'Well. [shrug] I suppose that is one way to see it.' --voice embry --allow-unknown-tags > "$OUT" 2>/dev/null; rc=$?; python3 - "$OUT" <<'PY'
import json,sys
res=json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
assert res.get('ok') is True, res
rec=json.load(open(res['receipt']))
assert rec.get('allow_unknown_tags') is True, rec.get('allow_unknown_tags')
assert any('shrug' in t for t in rec.get('unknown_tags_detected', [])), rec.get('unknown_tags_detected')
assert rec.get('unknown_tag_policy') == 'explicit_operator_opt_out', rec.get('unknown_tag_policy')
print('PASS_OPT_OUT_RECEIPT')
PY
test $rc -eq 0
expected_notes: explicit --allow-unknown-tags renders successfully through the live service
receipt records allow_unknown_tags=true, the detected [shrug] tag, and unknown_tag_policy=explicit_operator_opt_out

cases.name: zero-post-on-unknown-tag
command: cd /home/graham/workspace/experiments/agent-skills/skills/chatterbox-speak && export CHATTERBOX_SPEAK_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9; E1=$(mktemp /tmp/cbx-zp-tag-XXXX.err); E2=$(mktemp /tmp/cbx-zp-ctl-XXXX.err); ./run.sh speak --text 'Hello there. [shrug]' --voice embry > /dev/null 2>"$E1"; rc1=$?; grep -q 'shrug' "$E1" && ! grep -qiE 'connect|refused' "$E1" && test "$rc1" -eq 1 || { echo 'TAG_HALF_FAILED'; cat "$E1"; exit 1; }; ./run.sh speak --text 'Hello there plainly.' --voice embry > /dev/null 2>"$E2"; rc2=$?; test "$rc2" -ne 0 && grep -qiE 'connect|refused' "$E2" || { echo 'CONTROL_HALF_FAILED'; cat "$E2"; exit 1; }; echo PASS_ZERO_POST
expected_notes: with the service endpoint pinned to a closed port, an unknown tag fails with exit 1 naming the tag and NO connection error: the gate fires before any POST
paired control (valid text, same closed port) fails with a connection error instead, proving the override routes and a POST would otherwise have been attempted

proves: waveform-level affect evidence via analyze-chatterbox-emotions embedded in the receipt
does_not_prove: real speaker emotion or human-perceived quality (acoustic proxies only)
